title: KV key-schema economics, hit-rate modeling, TTL allocator, and graceful rollback
creator: Amina Patel
description: Goal: build an automated recommendation and safe-apply system that proposes KV/prefix cache key schema changes, per-prefix TTL allocations, and rollout/rollback controls based on hit-rate economics. This ticket covers: 1) a lightweight hit-rate synthesis model that converts sample access traces into per-prefix marginal-value curves, 2) a TTL allocator (heuristic + small optimizer) that maps economic tradeoffs (latency cost vs token savings) to TTL suggestions, 3) schema guidance and transformation checks for cache keys (avoid high-cardinality suffixing, canonicalization rules), and 4) a staged, observable apply+rollback protocol with automatic safety gates for runtime deploys. This work is intended to feed Redwood Optimize recommendations and the runtime config applier.
acceptance_criteria:
- The hit-rate model runs on a 7-day sample trace and produces per-prefix hit elasticity curves (CSV) for 95% of active prefixes.
- TTL allocator outputs a ranked list of TTL candidates with estimated cost delta and latency delta for each candidate.
- Cache key linter flags at least three classes of unsafe key patterns (high-cardinality suffixes, user-id embedding, non-deterministic timestamps).
- A canary pipeline exists that can apply a TTL/key change to 1%, 10%, 50% traffic buckets with shadow mode and produces rollback triggers when thresholds are breached.
- Rollback triggers are enforced automatically in staging and optionally in production when configured (see thresholds below).
- PR with implementation + unit/integration tests merged and e2e notebook demonstrating a safe rollout for a synthetic workload in the cost-optimizer repo.
implementation_plan: 1) Data ingestion: extend existing sampling job to emit prefix-level counts, TTLs, and observed hit outcomes (7-day rolling window). 2) Modeling: implement a small service (batch job) that fits an empirical hit curve per prefix (piecewise linear on log-scale) and computes marginal benefit vs TTL. 3) TTL allocator: implement greedy allocator that ranks prefixes by benefit-per-memory-token and proposes discrete TTLs (0s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h, 6h). 4) Key schema checks: implement linter with rules and automatic canonicalization suggestions (strip transient suffix patterns). 5) Safety control plane: add staged apply API to runtime config service supporting dry-run/shadow, canary percentages, metric hooks. 6) Auto-rollback: implement controller that watches configured metrics and triggers automated rollback or pause. 7) Integration: wire outputs to Redwood Optimize recommendations UI and provide CLI for ops to accept/reject proposals. 8) Docs & runbooks: write runbook for manual rollback and escalation steps.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for hit-curve fitting (edge cases: cold prefixes, heavy-tailed prefixes).
- Integration test: feed synthetic trace with known TTL-optimal solution and assert allocator suggestion matches ground truth within tolerance.
- Shadow testing: apply suggestions in shadow mode for 48h, compare observed vs predicted deltas.
- Chaos test: inject traffic spike and validate rollback automation triggers/pause behavior.
- Load test: verify config applier scales to 10k proposals/hour without exceeding control-plane QPS.
- Security review: verify linter prevents any proposal that would expose PII as cache keys.
rollout_and_rollback_steps:
Rollout plan: 1) Dry-run locally using notebook and small synthetic dataset. 2) Shadow apply for 48h across 100% traffic but without affecting serving decisions (metrics only). 3) Canary 1% traffic for 4h; monitor metrics. 4) If stable, ramp to 10% for 12h, then 50% for 12h, then 100%.
Automatic rollback triggers (configurable per-campaign):
- Global hit-rate drop: total effective cache hit-rate decreases >5% absolute vs baseline over 30m window -> immediate rollback.
- Latency regression: p95 request latency increases >15% vs baseline over 5m aggregated -> pause and alert.
- Cost anomaly: token-cost-per-minute increases >8% vs predicted -> rollback.
- Error spike: 5xx rate increases by 3x baseline or exceeds 0.5% -> rollback.
Manual rollback: ops can issue immediate rollback via Console or CLI; rollback must restore previous TTLs and key schema transforms and run a verification sweep.
Post-rollback checklist: collect traces, run model to find root cause, apply narrower TTL or revert key canonicalization if culprit identified.
metrics_to_monitor:
- per-prefix hit-rate (1m/5m/30m)
- global effective hit-rate and effective token savings
- p50/p95/p99 latency (overall + per-prefix hot-path)
- token-cost per minute and estimated projected savings
- 5xx and other error rates
- proposal acceptance rate and manual override frequency
- rollback frequency and mean-time-to-rollback
notes_and_decisions:
- We prioritize economic ROI: suggestions should only be surfaced when projected cost savings exceed operational risk (default minimum: $50/month per proposal).
- Key canonicalization will be opt-in by service; we will not auto-apply schema rewrites without explicit service owner approval.
- For cold prefixes (tail > 90% of prefixes), the allocator will prefer short TTLs or no caching.
- Use discrete TTL buckets to keep runtime metadata small and rollout atomic.
- Initial auto-rollback thresholds are conservative and will be loosened after two successful campaigns and historical calibration.
updates: 2025-01-20: Ticket created by Amina Patel. Scope reviewed with Product; agreed to split modeling and applier into separate sub-tasks if needed.

2025-01-25: Spike completed—collected 7-day sample traces from staging and validated schema variety. Found 3 common anti-patterns in keys: user-timestamp suffixing, fully hashed user IDs (blocking dedup), and embedded JWT fragments.
2025-01-30: First iteration of hit-curve fitter checked in (batch job). Early results: top 1% prefixes represent ~60% of cache value; long tail shows negligible per-prefix ROI.

2025-02-03: Linter prototype added to cost-optimizer repo; it flags patterns and suggests canonicalization. Discussed with DX and decided canonicalization is opt-in. Assignee: Diego to add CLI opt-in flow.
2025-02-05: Safety controller design doc merged; initial thresholds proposed (see rollout steps). Preparing PR for staged apply API. Next: implement shadow pipeline and integrate with metrics hooks.
